dingy|disconsolate.distinction: A dingy room is dirty and depressing to look at, while a disconsolate person is the one sitting in it beyond comforting.

dirge|elegy.distinction: A dirge is sung at the graveside, an elegy is written and read; the dirge is music, the elegy is verse.

disaffected|malcontent.distinction: Disaffected describes loyalty that has curdled, while a malcontent is the person who has been complaining all along.

discomfit|disconcert.distinction: To discomfit someone is to leave them embarrassed and at a loss, while to disconcert them is to throw their composure off for a moment.

discount|dismiss.distinction: You discount evidence by giving it less weight than it deserves, and dismiss it by refusing to weigh it at all.

discount|disregard.distinction: To discount a claim is to count it for less, while to disregard it is to act as though it had never been made.

discrepancy|variance.distinction: A discrepancy is two figures that ought to match and do not, while a variance is the measured size of the gap between them.

discriminating|incisive.distinction: A discriminating palate tells fine things apart, while an incisive question cuts to the heart of a matter in one stroke.

discriminating|keen.distinction: Discriminating taste notices fine differences, while a keen eye simply misses nothing; one sorts, the other spots.

disdain|scorn.distinction: Disdain looks down in cold silence, while scorn says so out loud; disdain withholds respect, scorn actively mocks.

disinterested|impartial.distinction: A disinterested judge has nothing to gain from the outcome, while an impartial one shows no favour whichever way they lean.

dismiss|disregard.distinction: To dismiss a proposal is to reject it outright, while to disregard it is to leave it lying unanswered.

disperse|dissipate.distinction: A crowd disperses when it scatters in all directions, while a fortune dissipates when it scatters until nothing is left.

disport|gambol.distinction: To disport oneself is to take pleasure at leisure, while to gambol is to skip and leap like a lamb in a field.

disregard|snub.distinction: To disregard someone is simply not to notice them, while to snub them is to make the not noticing unmistakable.

dissembler|phony.distinction: A dissembler hides real motives behind a convincing front, while a phony has no substance behind the front at all.

dissemble|feign.distinction: To dissemble is to hide the feeling you actually have, while to feign is to display a feeling you do not have.

dissident|heretical.distinction: A dissident is a person who opposes the official line, while heretical describes the belief itself as against doctrine.

dissident|heterodox.distinction: A dissident opposes the authorities openly, while heterodox describes an opinion that simply departs from the accepted one.

distort|garble.distinction: To distort a message is to bend its meaning on purpose, while to garble it is to scramble it so no meaning survives.

dogged|pertinacious.distinction: Dogged persistence is admired for its endurance, while pertinacious persistence irritates because it will not let go.

dogged|tenacious.distinction: Dogged effort keeps plodding forward, while a tenacious grip simply refuses to release what it already holds.

dolorous|lachrymose.distinction: Dolorous describes grief in the voice or the scene, while lachrymose describes the tears, whether shed or provoked.

dulcet|mellifluous.distinction: Dulcet tones are sweet and soothing to hear, while mellifluous ones flow smoothly like honey; sweetness against smoothness.

ebullient|exuberant.distinction: Ebullient spirits bubble up in the moment, while exuberant energy grows and spills over abundantly.

eclipse|overshadow.distinction: To eclipse a rival is to surpass them outright, while to overshadow them is to loom so large they go unnoticed.

economical|frugal.distinction: An economical method wastes nothing, while a frugal person chooses to spend little; one is efficient, the other abstemious.

economical|sparing.distinction: Economical use gets full value from what is spent, while sparing use simply parts with as little as possible.

economical|stinting.distinction: An economical budget avoids waste, while a stinting one grudges what it hands over; the first is prudent, the second mean.

effervescent|scintillating.distinction: An effervescent manner bubbles with cheerful energy, while scintillating talk sparkles with cleverness.

effrontery|gall.distinction: Effrontery is shameless boldness with a formal ring, while gall is the same nerve described with contempt.

effrontery|presumption.distinction: Effrontery is brazen and knows it, while presumption is the quieter arrogance of assuming a right one does not have.

egregious|flagrant.distinction: An egregious error stands out for how bad it is, while a flagrant one stands out for being committed openly.

elaborate|expatiate.distinction: Elaborate describes a design worked out in fine detail, while to expatiate is to go on at length about a subject.

elaborate|expound.distinction: An elaborate plan is intricate in its construction, while to expound a plan is to set it out at length for an audience.

elated|jubilant.distinction: Elated describes spirits lifted high by good news, while jubilant adds the triumph and the noise of celebration.

elicit|evoke.distinction: You elicit an answer by asking for it, while a smell evokes a memory without anyone asking anything.

elicit|kindle.distinction: To elicit a response is to draw it out of someone, while to kindle interest is to set it alight where there was none.

elicit|provoke.distinction: To elicit a reaction is to draw it out deliberately, while to provoke one is to goad until it bursts out.

eloquent|facile.distinction: Eloquent speech is fluent and moves people, while facile speech is fluent and has nothing underneath it.
